title: Capcom Showed Resident Evil 7 a Year Early and Nobody Knew
hook: At E3 2015 Capcom let people play a VR demo called Kitchen with no Resident Evil logo on it. A year later it turned out to be Resident Evil 7, and the T in the Kitchen logo had been cut to look like a 7 the whole time. Did you play Kitchen before you knew what it was?
script: Did you know Capcom showed Resident Evil Seven to the public a full year before anyone knew what it was? At E3 in June of two thousand fifteen, Capcom brought a short virtual reality demo to Sony's booth. It was called Kitchen. You sat tied to a chair in a filthy kitchen while something horrible happened right in front of you. Capcom said only that it ran on a new engine that did not have a name yet. There was no Resident Evil logo anywhere, and the press could only guess at a connection. Then, at Sony's E3 press conference in June of two thousand sixteen, Resident Evil Seven was finally revealed to the world. Capcom confirmed that Kitchen had been built on its new RE Engine as a test for the game. Watching terrified players at E3 convinced them that horror and VR belonged together. Looking back, fans noticed the letter T in the Kitchen logo was cut to look like a seven. Resident Evil Seven launched in January of two thousand seventeen as the first numbered entry in first person. The entire game was playable in PlayStation VR. Its free demo passed three million downloads before launch, and the game has since sold more than seventeen million copies. Did you try Kitchen without knowing what it was? Follow for more gaming history.
